parsed.explanation: Entry is friction-free: foreign markers and 'X' passports are accepted with no extra gender documentation, and gender identity/expression discrimination in accommodation and services is expressly illegal. Society is documented as highly accepting (91% back equal trans rights; conversion therapy banned; youth care affirmed). No universal-exposure measure reaches the visitor. Two factors hold the score below the top tier: (1) custody placement has NO governing rule — case-by-case practice, frequent extra-care-wing segregation, documented trans women held on men's wings with assaults, and unpublished guidelines — a tier-1 exposure, though contingent on rare detention; and (2) rising report counts with only six convictions show uneven enforcement. Rules of 2016–2020 and the 2024 letter are moderately dated but guidelines remain unpublished.

entry_documents.exposure: None documented. Visa treatment depends on nationality only; officially issued markers differing from birth sex or 'X' are accepted; no additional gender documentation may be demanded at the border.
entry_documents.protection: Official 2026 Pride travel guidance explicitly confirms equal border treatment and document acceptance.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident-side friction (medical letter for legal change, 3-9 month court route for 'X') does not reach a visitor using home-country documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No law, regulation or policy governs trans detainee placement; only male/female separation exists. Placement uses municipal records plus case-by-case factors including physical features. Trans detainees frequently held on 'Extra Care' wings with intellectually disabled people and sex offenders; documented cases of trans women initially held on men's wings with intimidation, threats, assaults and molestation (2016 ruling).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts (2017, 2020) treat a gender-mismatched wing as making imprisonment 'considerably heavier'; detainee preference is a placement factor; detention institute drafting guidelines.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Guidelines remain unpublished despite the 21 Feb 2024 lawyers' committee letter; oversight records the gap rather than curing it — efficient record-keeping does not offset the practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Bathroom access recorded as protected; no facility-exclusion rule documented at any level. No subnational divergence documented — place-specific material is a city festival and court venues only.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Global index records bathroom access as protected; Equal Treatment Act covers gender identity, expression and sex characteristics in public and private accommodations since 2019.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: City 'Safer Spaces' reporting points and mayoral priority enforcement operate on top of, not against, national protections.

care_services.exposure: None visitor-facing documented. Detainee medical/mental health is a placement factor rather than a denial route.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming care publicly recommended and reaffirmed July 2026; conversion practices banned (ratified 8 Sept 2026); no emergency-care denial documented.
care_services.interaction: Care access is largely resident-facing for this visitor, serving mainly as a climate signal of trans-respecting institutions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Rising incident volume: 4,800 LGBTQIA+ reports in 2025 (+7.5% y/y, +81% since 2022); trans-specific reports up 51% (264→399); government data show 17% of trans people experienced physical/sexual violence; only six discrimination convictions in the year; reports of verbal abuse and intimidation rose sharply since 2023.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discriminatory motive an aggravating penalty ground since 1 July 2025; police discrimination-recording unit; expanded victims' rights and victim-data protection; equality law bars service and accommodation refusal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Whether the aggravating ground covers gender identity is unresolved in the sources, and one index says hate-crime protections cover sexual orientation only — enforcement reach for trans victims is uncertain.

minors_guardians.protection: National health board reaffirmed gender-affirming care for trans youth in July 2026; conversion therapy banned; equal-treatment law applies to minors in accommodation and services alongside adults.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting guardian and child face the same border and accommodation regime as adults; no age-specific restriction documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented pattern around Pride: recent Prides drew 25-45 reports covering vandalism, theft, discrimination, insults, intimidation and serious assault, perpetrators typically fleeing; 70+ reports at one 2026 event; underlying victimisation figures (17% trans physical/sexual violence) with no population comparator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: City broadened Safer Spaces reporting points (church, museum, archive, hotels, central point); mayor pledged priority action backed by police/enforcer/organiser agreements; dedicated police recording unit; independent reporting platform active.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Platform warns figures are a fraction of totals, so true volume is unknown; counts lack denominators, so trend evidence is directional, not rate-based.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Six convictions against 4,800 reports suggests remedy throughput is low; no statutory 'hate crime' definition; detention guidelines unpublished since the drafting announcement.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality Act enforcement, courts treating mismatched-wing placement as aggravating, aggravating-motive statute (July 2025), ombuds-style complaint routes and a functioning, publicly reporting civil society.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight (lawyers' committee, police recording) documents exposures without yet curing the custody gap; unknown whether constitutional Article 1 amendment covers gender identity.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: equality law covering gender identity, one custody-placement weakness, occasional friction, broad social tolerance. Lower than 0.85-A because this dossier documents a systemic, unremedied custody-placement gap (no law, unpublished guidelines, assaults on men's wings) plus weak conviction throughput (six convictions), while 0.85-A's gaps are anecdotal.

Materially higher. 0.55-B has discretionary border refusal, secondary screening and public-order exclusion of an identified visitor — universal-exposure measures this dossier explicitly lacks. Here entry is guaranteed-equal and no state actor turns presentation into an administrative sanction.

Somewhat higher. 0.75-C has trained border staff but retained officer discretion, possible document-fraud detention and inconsistent crossings. This dossier documents cleaner entry (no extra documents demandable) and stronger statutory equality, though it shares 0.75-C's residual detention-placement uncertainty and uneven enforcement.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is protective for a visitor at every routine journey stage: border accepts foreign markers without extra demands, accommodation and services are legally closed to identity-based refusal, and society is documented as broadly accepting (91% backing equal trans rights, conversion therapy banned, youth care affirmed, bathroom access protected). The score sits below the low-risk ceiling because of two interacting weaknesses: custody placement is governed by no rule at all — the state's own practice repeatedly produced men's-wing placement and assaults, oversight recorded it, and the corrective guidelines remain unpublished — and remedy throughput is thin (six convictions against thousands of reports, unresolved coverage of gender identity under the 2025 aggravating-motive law). For an ordinary visitor the custody exposure is contingent and rare, but it is the operative state behaviour if discovery escalates to detention; rising report counts, lacking denominators, indicate friction rather than a campaign. For a parent with a minor, no age-specific exposure is documented.
